land.text: the same land: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Brittany shape for 825-859 is the 24,213 km2 outline of this row's 602-771 shape

successors.note: The Kingdom of Brittany page lists Cornouaille, Domnonée, Broërec and the Marches of Neustria as predecessor states; Wihomarc's 'successful rebellion against Frankish rule' ran 822-825.

capitals.name: Vannes (Gwened)
capitals.note: Label point only, confidence 1: no page opened names a capital of the Breton kingdoms; the Bretons page says only that Bro Waroc'h 'dominated the region of Vannes (Gwened)'. Domnonée and Cornouaille had their own seats, unnamed on these pages.

keyframe_review.note: 24,348 km2 for 587-601 (86 cells). Page infobox of 'History of Brittany' gives 34,023 km2 for Brittany as a whole (ratio 0.72, within a factor of two). A gazetteer comparison (my check) shows the shape holds all of modern Côtes-d'Armor and Finistère, 18 of 25 cells of Morbihan, 11 of 30 of Ille-et-Vilaine and none of Loire-Atlantique, i.e. it leaves out the Rennes and Nantes borderland that 'the neighbouring Frankish kingdom created ... incorporating the counties of Rennes and Nantes' (History of Brittany, undated). The Bretons page: 'Brittany was divided into three kingdoms' (Domnonée, Cornouaille, Bro Waroc'h) and the migration ran 'most heavily from 450 to 600'. Unverified: the five pages opened (Bretons, History of Brittany, Breton March, Kingdom of Brittany, Brittany) are silent on this shape and the page budget is spent. Shape stands.

24,213 km2 (85 cells), one cell fewer than 587-601; nothing on the pages explains a change in 602. Unverified: the five pages opened (Bretons, History of Brittany, Breton March, Kingdom of Brittany, Brittany) are silent on this shape and the page budget is spent. Shape stands for 602-771.

24,440 km2 for 772-774, one cell different from the 602 and 775 outlines: a drafting artefact, not a border move; no page dates anything in 772-774. Unverified: the five pages opened (Bretons, History of Brittany, Breton March, Kingdom of Brittany, Brittany) are silent on this shape and the page budget is spent.

Back to the 602 outline for 775-813. No Frankish campaign of Charlemagne's reign is dated on any page opened; the Kingdom of Brittany page says only 'From 801 to 837, the adjacent Frankish Empire made several unsuccessful attempts to subdue the Breton tribes', i.e. no border move. Unverified: the five pages opened (Bretons, History of Brittany, Breton March, Kingdom of Brittany, Brittany) are silent on this shape and the page budget is spent.

Shape unchanged for 814-824. The Kingdom of Brittany page's list gives Morman as 'first ruler named King of Brittany by the Breton nobles upon the death of Charlemagne in 814', defeated by Louis the Pious (undated), a 'Period of Frankish rule under Louis the Pious' (819-822) and Wihomarc's 'successful rebellion against Frankish rule' (822-825). The shape is therefore the Breton land throughout, hatched as Frankish-occupied for 819-822 by the ledger's occupation events, not redrawn.

region.text: the three Breton kingdoms of western Armorica as Cliopatria draws them from 587

ledger.note: 587: Cliopatria's first Breton shape. The pages date no founding: the Bretons 'migrated in waves from the 3rd to 9th century (most heavily from 450 to 600) to the west of Armorica' and 'In the Early Middle Ages, Brittany was divided into three kingdoms ... Domnonée, Cornouaille (Kernev), and Bro Waroc'h (Broërec)'. 587 is Cliopatria's year, confidence 1.

region.text: Brittany under 'Frankish rule under Louis the Pious', 819-822

ledger.note: 819: Frankish rule over Brittany under Louis the Pious. The Kingdom of Brittany page's ruler list has a 'Period of Frankish rule under Louis the Pious' dated 819-822 after Morman 'rebelled against Frankish rule but was defeated by Louis the Pious' (no date given). Hatched Frankish occupation, not annexation: the Bretons keep a shape in Cliopatria and Nominoë, 'a noble Briton', is made 'head of the region' (undated).

region.text: Brittany, Frankish rule ended by Wihomarc's rebellion

ledger.note: 822: Wihomarc's rebellion. The ruler list gives Wihomarc as ruling 822-825 and 'led a successful rebellion against Frankish rule to re-establish Breton rule'. 822 is the start of his reign on the page; the revolt's own date is not given.

region.text: the Breton land, passing unchanged to the Kingdom of Brittany row

ledger.note: 824: Cliopatria's Breton Kingdoms row ends and its Kingdom of Brittany row begins in 825 on the same 24,213 km2 outline. A bookkeeping change of label; the pages date Wihomarc 822-825 and give no 824/825 event. Confidence 1.

wars.name: Frankish attempts to subdue the Bretons
wars.outcome: 'From 801 to 837, the adjacent Frankish Empire made several unsuccessful attempts to subdue the Breton tribes' (Kingdom of Brittany page); the only dated Frankish rule is 819-822, ended by Wihomarc's revolt.
wars.note: The Merovingian and Carolingian efforts 'from the sixth to ninth centuries ... to integrate the region into the Frankish kingdom' (History of Brittany) are undated on the pages. No individual campaign is named or dated on the pages opened. No zone: the Frankish Breton March borderland of Rennes and Nantes is undated. [Reviewer eu-07-c, 2026-10-24: 'to' clipped from 837 to the dossier's end (824); the page's war is 801-837 and continues under kingdom-of-brittany.]

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line in the period: the eastern frontier with the Franks (the Rennes and Nantes borderland) is approximate throughout; the other edges are the sea.

notes: Pages: all five opened pages (the budget) are thin for 587-824; no page dates a border move, so every Cliopatria shape is kept (verdict ok, unverified) and the ledger holds only the birth, the dated 819-822 Frankish rule (Kingdom of Brittany page) and the 824 hand-over. A gap filler should try 'Waroch II', 'Judicael', 'Morvan Lez-Breizh', 'Wihomarc', 'Nominoë' and 'Domnonée' for: the Merovingian and early Carolingian submissions of the Breton rulers, Charlemagne's and Louis the Pious's Breton campaigns, and any tribute that should be a vassal_start on the Frankish dossier (none of these is dated on the pages opened). Cliopatria merges three kingdoms (Domnonée, Cornouaille, Bro Waroc'h) into one row; separate dossiers are not required by the brief and no page gave their separate extents. The Frankish borderland of Rennes and Nantes (History of Brittany) is probably the older Breton march that the Breton March page says was 'created and militarized under the Merovingians in the late 7th or early 8th century' (my reading); it is not in this shape and belongs to the Frankish dossier. Gazetteer: no names needed (the shape is referenced through Cliopatria). The wikidata Q309197 is Cliopatria's. Rulers omitted: only Morman (814) and Wihomarc (822-825) are dated on the pages.
